summary: Tankers burn in Hormuz as Trump threatens Iran, Nvidia's founder quits, and Netanyahu's rival gets the first shot at governing Israel.

stories.headline: Tankers burn in Hormuz as Trump threatens new strikes on Iran
stories.dek: Iran says the ships ignored its warnings. Trump says he no longer needs a deal.
what: Iran says two supertankers carrying over 4 million barrels of oil were disabled by explosions on a Hormuz route it calls unauthorised.
Trump said the US no longer needs a deal with Iran and he would strike again "without hesitation", possibly right away.
Israeli media say the US military has told Israel to prepare for renewed action.
background: The US and Israel attacked Iran on 28 February. An April ceasefire didn't hold, and the fight moved to the Strait of Hormuz, where the US now blockades Iranian ports.
stories.why: About a fifth of the world's oil passes through Hormuz. Trouble there pushes up fuel and food prices everywhere.
stories.say: The Iran war never really ended. It just moved to the Strait of Hormuz.

terms.def: The narrow sea passage between Iran and Oman. It is the world's key oil chokepoint.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard, an elite force separate from the regular army.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang quits as Nvidia CEO after 33 years
stories.dek: Finance chief Colette Kress takes over for now, after a spy scandal.
what: Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, has resigned. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board looks for a permanent one.
It follows a board probe into his affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US officials reportedly suspect of spying for Beijing.
Nvidia says it has no reason to think company secrets or national security were compromised.
background: Nvidia makes the chips behind most of the world's AI and is worth over $4 trillion. The US bans sales of its best chips to China.
stories.why: Nvidia is at the centre of the AI boom and the US–China tech fight. Losing its founder like this shakes both.
stories.say: Nvidia lost the founder who built it into the engine of AI, over a national-security scandal.

terms.def: A temporary boss who runs a company until a permanent one is chosen.

stories.headline: Netanyahu's rival Eisenkot gets first shot at forming Israel's government
stories.dek: The former army chief has 28 days to build a working majority.
what: President Herzog gave the mandate to Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar party, passing over Prime Minister Netanyahu.
67 of 120 lawmakers backed him, but that includes Arab-led parties some of his partners won't rely on.
He has 28 days, plus a possible 14. If he fails, Netanyahu gets a turn.
background: Israel voted on 27 October. No party ever wins alone, so governments are coalitions that need 61 of the Knesset's 120 seats.
stories.why: This could end the Netanyahu era. The next government will set Israel's course on Gaza and Iran.
stories.say: Eisenkot has the mandate, but he still needs 61 reliable votes to replace Netanyahu.

stories.headline: G7 warns China over its pressure east of Taiwan
stories.dek: Taipei fears Beijing's coast-guard patrols are rehearsals for a blockade.
what: G7 foreign ministers, meeting in Paris, said China's activity east of Taiwan threatens regional stability and international shipping.
It is their strongest joint statement on it yet. Beijing called it interference in its internal affairs.
background: China claims Taiwan and hasn't ruled out force. Since June its coast guard has patrolled Taiwan's Pacific coast, the side Taipei relies on for supplies in a crisis.
stories.why: Taiwan makes most of the world's advanced chips. A blockade could cut it off without a shot being fired.
stories.say: The fear over Taiwan has shifted from invasion to blockade.

terms.def: Seven big democratic economies: the US, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and Canada.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine hold first US-brokered talks in nine months
stories.dek: The Abu Dhabi talks were called productive, but the strikes go on.
what: Delegations met in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November, with Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner mediating.
US Secretary of State Rubio called the talks very productive but said much work remains. Russia objects to Europe taking part.
background: Russia invaded in February 2022. The front is largely stuck and both sides keep up long-range strikes. Russia fired 162 drones the night before talks began.
stories.why: It's the first real diplomacy in months, but territory is still the sticking point.
stories.say: Russia and Ukraine are talking again, but neither side has moved on territory.

terms.def: Promises from other countries to help defend Ukraine if Russia attacks again after a deal.

stories.headline: Democrats win the Senate, then fight over who leads it
stories.dek: Chris Van Hollen is moving to challenge Chuck Schumer.
what: The 3 November midterms gave Democrats control of the Senate from January, which would make Schumer majority leader again.
Several Democrats won't back him. NPR reports Maryland's Chris Van Hollen now says he'll challenge him, and Elissa Slotkin is weighing a run.
background: Each party's senators pick their leader in a closed majority vote, expected next month. The majority leader controls which bills get a vote.
stories.why: The winner decides how Democrats use their majority against Trump, from investigations to the Iran war.
stories.say: Democrats won the Senate and immediately started fighting over whether Schumer should lead it.

terms.def: US elections held halfway through a president's term.

stories.headline: US inflation runs hot, and a Fed rate hike looks likely
stories.dek: Prices rose 0.4% in October, the last big reading before the Fed meets.
what: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% expected. Core prices, without food and energy, rose 0.3%.
There's no annual figure: last year's shutdown meant October 2025 prices were never collected. September's annual rate was 3.7%.
background: The Fed targets 2% inflation. With prices well above that, markets expect a rate hike at its 8–9 December meeting, not a cut.
stories.why: Higher US rates make borrowing more expensive and ripple through markets worldwide.
stories.say: US inflation is stuck well above target, so the Fed is expected to raise rates, not cut them.

terms.def: Price rises without food and energy, which swing a lot. It shows the underlying trend.

stories.headline: COP31 climate talks hit halfway in Antalya, without the US
stories.dek: Leaders have spoken. The fight over money runs until 20 November.
what: About 190 countries are meeting in Antalya, Turkey. Turkey hosts while Australia runs the negotiations.
The hosts want a pledge to electrify over a third of the global economy by 2035.
The US sent no officials after Trump took it out of the Paris Agreement.
background: COPs are the yearly UN climate summits. Poorer countries want more money to cope with climate change, and the EU says there's little appetite for new pledges.
stories.why: The world is off track for the 1.5°C goal, and these deals shape energy prices for years.
stories.say: COP31 is going ahead without the US, so it's up to Europe, China and emerging economies.

stories.headline: SpaceX plans to retire Crew Dragon, America's astronaut taxi
stories.dek: It's betting on Starship, leaving NASA leaning on Boeing.
what: SpaceX will wind down Falcon 9 and Crew Dragon around 2030, when the space station retires, NASA's chief has confirmed.
NASA is paying Boeing $359 million to revive Starliner, whose only crewed flight ended with its astronauts coming home on a SpaceX capsule.
background: Since 2020, Crew Dragon has been the main way NASA gets astronauts to the space station.
stories.why: The West's access to space increasingly depends on one company's business choices.
stories.say: SpaceX is retiring NASA's taxi to bet on Starship, and NASA's plan B is Boeing.

briefs.text: Trump warned Mexico over a migrant caravan heading north. Mexico's President Sheinbaum says migrants are being sent home.
Brazil's Lula, fresh from re-election, is among the leaders speaking at COP31.
Today, 13 November, is World Kindness Day.
